In Matplotlib, the `figure.figsize` parameter is used to specify the default size of figures created. It takes a tuple of two values, representing the width and height of the figure in inches. Adjusting this parameter allows you to control the size of your plots more effectively. 

Here's how to set this parameter and create a figure with the specified size:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Set the default figure size
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = [10, 5]  # Width: 10 inches, Height: 5 inches

# Create some sample data
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
y = np.sin(x)

# Create a plot
plt.plot(x, y)
plt.title('Sine Wave')
plt.xlabel('X-axis')
plt.ylabel('Y-axis')
plt.grid()
plt.show()
```

In this example, the figure size will be set to 10 inches wide and 5 inches tall. The output will display a sine wave plot with the specified dimensions. You can easily adjust the figure size by modifying the values in the tuple assigned to `figure.figsize`. 

If you want to set the figure size for a single figure without changing the default configuration, you can do it directly in the `figure` function as shown below:

```python
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))  # Set figure size for this specific plot
plt.plot(x, y, color='r')
plt.title('Sine Wave')
plt.xlabel('X-axis')
plt.ylabel('Y-axis')
plt.grid()
plt.show()
```

This method allows for more flexibility when working with multiple plots of varying sizes in the same script.
